author: Thoughty2
description:
Ignaz Semmelweis made a discovery so simple it feels like it should come with a “no brainer” warning, and yet it was ignored for decades. Working at Vienna General Hospital, he noticed women were far more likely to die of childbed fever in the ward run by doctors than the one run by midwives… but why?

He realised doctors were going straight from autopsies to delivering babies. When he introduced the revolutionary idea of handwashing between the two, deaths plummeted almost overnight.

However, without a more scientific explanation than “they had death on their hands”, Semmelweis’ discovery was met with ridicule rather than the gratitude it deserved, and many more lives would be lost before germ theory finally offered an explanation for why Semmelweis’ idea worked.
title: The Medical Breakthrough They All Laughed At
